subject.title: Session `status` field values ("failed", "timeout", "done") mislead agents into spawning duplicate sessions

question: Should OpenClaw solve this by adding an additive resumability/status-semantics signal to `sessions_list`, and if so should `killed` and shared Gateway rows be treated as resumable?
rationale: Current code proves the ambiguity remains, but the previous clean fix path closed unmerged because the durable API contract and client-visible scope were still maintainer choices.

options.title: Add backward-compatible resumability metadata
options.body: Define `resumable` semantics for known non-running statuses, update agent-facing guidance, and preserve existing `status` values for compatibility.

options.title: Limit the hint to agent tooling
options.body: Keep Gateway row contracts unchanged and add only model-facing `sessions_list` output/guidance if maintainers do not want a client-visible field.

options.title: Redesign lifecycle status names
options.body: Rename or split status semantics only with an explicit breaking-change/migration plan for existing API and prompt consumers.

recommendation.title: Add backward-compatible resumability metadata
recommendation.body: Define `resumable` semantics for known non-running statuses, update agent-facing guidance, and preserve existing `status` values for compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses Gateway row contract, agent prompt semantics, and recent session-surface ownership, where steipete has recent and historical routing evidence.
